title: Game Network Endpoint Classification
summary: The game client uses multiple independent network paths: HTTP (via WININET/WinHTTP), raw TCP sockets (WS2_32), and local named-pipe IPC (NESYS). Each feature maps to a distinct transport.

network_paths.notes: UE4 HTTP layer (HttpWinInet.cpp) routes HTTP over WININET.dll. This is the primary operator-visible HTTP interface to the game.
Direct TCP socket path used for matching and battle coordination with the GameServer. Separate from HTTP path.

The game imports both server-side (ConnectNamedPipe) and client-side pipe functions. Whether the game is pipe server or client requires control-flow analysis. GALAXYIO.dll handles HTTP (WinHTTP) and USB, not the pipe.
GALAXYIO.dll contacts production NESYS certificate endpoints. These are production-trust dependencies, NOT reproduced by a private server.

private_server_interface_evidence.notice: The current private server exposes fixed interfaces (HTTP :4001, proxy :80, TCP :6666). Game-side evidence is required before claiming the game uses these. This artifact does NOT assume the game targets these interfaces.

proxy_80.game_side_evidence: Hardcoded URL dev.starwing.jp/mock uses default HTTP port 80. Hosts-file redirection (previously used) requires operator action, NOT a confirmed game-side override.

endpoint_override.detail: No supported game-side configuration exists to redirect the game to a private-server endpoint via command line, INI, UE4 config, environment variable, Registry, XML, JSON, or binary config. The only practical redirect is operator-level hosts-file/DNS override, which is out of scope for G19.

analysis_method: Static analysis of PE imports and strings
notes: The game uses multiple independent network paths (HTTP + TCP + local pipe)
HTTP is the primary operator-visible interface
TCP is used for matching/battle coordination
Local pipe is used for NESYS card operations
GALAXYIO.dll handles production certificate/HTTP, not the local pipe
No supported endpoint override exists in game configuration
